name: The Traffic Cone That Stood Up
brief: The very first waking: a battered orange traffic cone on a torn up Delancey Street lifts itself onto two newly grown legs of rebar and reflective tape while a road crew freezes mid swing, the jackhammer still ringing, an eye flower unfolding from its crown like a periscope, steam and sparks caught in the streetlight, color story: cone safety orange and asphalt slate over ink black

name: The Scaffold That Walked
brief: A sidewalk shed that has covered the same Upper West Side block for eleven years pulls its plywood legs free and takes one enormous step, pedestrians scattering into a rain of pigeon feathers and permit dust, eye flowers opening along every green painted joint, its shadow moving for the first time, color story: shed green and construction lamp gold over ink black

name: The Mannequin in the Broken Window
brief: A cracked storefront mannequin in a shuttered Fifth Avenue window turns its head toward a girl who stopped to look, its blank face splitting open into a single enormous iris, the security gate half rolled and casting bars of light across both of them, color story: mannequin bisque and gate steel blue over ink black

name: The Crossing Signal Learns to Beg
brief: A pedestrian crossing signal at a Queens intersection climbs down its own pole on cable arms and holds its lit hand out to a woman waiting to cross, the countdown numbers replaced by a slow blinking eye flower, cars stopped in both directions with headlights blazing, color story: signal white hand and taillight red over ink black

name: The Statue That Blinked First
brief: A weathered bronze figure in a small Brooklyn triangle park blinks green oxidised eyelids for the first time in a hundred and twenty years while a chess hustler drops a rook and does not pick it up, eye flowers pushing out of the verdigris in the folds of the coat, color story: bronze verdigris and park lamp amber over ink black

name: The Payphone Remembers Every Call
brief: The last standing payphone husk on a Harlem corner rears up on coiled steel cord legs and every call it ever carried plays at once as a chorus of overlapping voices made visible in the vapour, eye flowers blooming from the coin return, a man frozen with his key in a door across the street, color story: receiver chrome and voice vapour violet over ink black

name: The Umbrella That Refused the Bin
brief: A broken umbrella climbs out of an overflowing Midtown trash can on bent spokes and opens itself into a wobbling canopy over a drenched delivery rider who did not ask for help, an eye flower unfurling at the ferrule, rain sheeting sideways under a bus shelter light, color story: umbrella black and downpour silver over ink black

name: The Shopping Cart Chose a Direction
brief: An abandoned shopping cart at the bottom of a Bronx hill rights itself, corrects its bad wheel with a shudder and rolls uphill against gravity while three kids sprint after it whooping, eye flowers opening in the wire lattice, dusk sky burning behind the elevated tracks, color story: cart nickel silver and Bronx dusk tangerine over ink black

name: The Fire Escape Flexed
brief: An iron fire escape peels off a Lower East Side tenement face like a limb waking from sleep, curling down to lower a stranded cat to the sidewalk while the whole block leans out of windows, eye flowers opening on every rusted tread, laundry lines snapping in the draft, color story: rust iron red and tenement brick over ink black

name: The Dumpster With Opinions
brief: A restaurant dumpster in a Hell's Kitchen alley heaves its lid open and slams it twice in unmistakable disapproval at a man about to dump paint cans, an eye flower rising on a stalk from inside the trash, rats holding position on both walls like an audience, color story: dumpster forest green and alley sodium gold over ink black

name: The Bollard That Would Not Move
brief: A steel bollard outside a Chelsea school plants itself deeper into the pavement as a runaway van bears down, concrete cracking outward in a star from its base, an eye flower flaring open at its cap in the instant before impact, crossing guard mid shout, color story: bollard safety yellow and van headlight white over ink black

name: The Water Tower Sat Up
brief: A wooden rooftop water tower unfolds its legs and sits up on a Tribeca roof like a giant waking at dawn, spilling a curtain of water off its brim over the parapet, an enormous eye flower opening in its hatch, the skyline behind it turning gold in one strip, color story: cedar stave brown and dawn spill silver over ink black

name: The Slicer Who Knows Your Order
brief: A bodega deli slicer leans off the counter on articulated arms and starts a hero sandwich for a regular before he has finished walking in, blade spinning into a disc of light, an eye flower opening in the guard housing, the cat asleep on the register unbothered, color story: slicer steel and pastrami rose over ink black

name: The Coffee Urn at Four Fifteen
brief: A dented steel coffee urn pours itself for the first customer of the morning without being touched, steam curling into the shape of a face that dissolves, eye flowers opening in the sight glass, a night shift nurse and a day shift mason meeting eyes across the counter, color story: urn steel and coffee amber over ink black

name: The Lottery Terminal Feels Guilty
brief: A scratch off lottery terminal shivers on the counter and physically withholds a ticket from a shaking regular, printing a blank slip instead, an eye flower opening in its ticket slot looking genuinely sorry, the man's reflection doubled in the plexiglass, color story: ticket paper pink and terminal display green over ink black

name: The Bodega Cat Cam
brief: The dusty ceiling security camera in a Washington Heights bodega swivels away from the register and follows the cat instead, its lens iris turning into a living eye flower, four monitors behind the counter all showing the same cat from different years, color story: monitor phosphor green and dust mote gold over ink black

name: The Cooler Door Holds a Grudge
brief: The glass cooler door seals itself shut against a customer who has been putting warm drinks back on the shelf for a decade, condensation forming a perfect iris on the inside of the glass, other customers pretending very hard not to notice, color story: cooler light cyan and condensation silver over ink black

name: The Chopped Cheese Griddle
brief: A blackened flat top griddle in an uptown bodega works its own spatula in a blur while a line of construction workers watches in silence, onions and beef throwing a fan of steam, an eye flower opening in the grease trap catching the fluorescent tube overhead, color story: griddle carbon black and onion caramel gold over ink black

name: The Change Machine Gives Extra
brief: A laundromat change machine on Fordham Road quietly overpays a mother counting singles, coins arcing out in a slow bright rope she has to cup both hands to catch, an eye flower opening in the coin slot, dryers turning behind her like planets, color story: quarter nickel silver and laundromat fluorescent mint over ink black

name: The Halal Cart Ignited Itself
brief: A halal cart on a Midtown corner lights its own burners at dusk and begins prepping before its owner arrives, tongs and knives moving in practiced sequence, eye flowers blooming in the steam tray vapour, a line already forming out of pure instinct, color story: cart stainless and saffron gold over ink black

name: The Ice Machine Dreams of Alaska
brief: A wheezing ice machine in a Sunset Park basement produces a single perfect glacier blue block with a whole miniature frozen coastline inside it, an eye flower suspended at its centre, the delivery kid staring at it with the door still open, color story: glacier blue and basement bulb amber over ink black

name: The Flower Bucket Out Front
brief: The galvanised bucket of cellophane roses outside a corner store tips itself toward a man who has walked past it four nights running, the flowers all turning to face him at once with living irises, rain starting on the awning above, color story: cellophane rose red and galvanised bucket gray over ink black

name: The Bell Above the Door
brief: The small brass bell over a Greenpoint bodega door rings itself in a pattern the owner recognises as his mother's name, freezing him with a case of eggs in his arms, an eye flower opening inside the bell mouth, dust suspended in the doorway light, color story: brass bell gold and doorway daylight white over ink black

name: The Milk Crate Throne
brief: A stack of milk crates outside a Bed Stuy store assembles itself into a proper throne and waits, and the oldest man on the block sits down in it like he always knew this day would come, eye flowers opening through every crate slot, the whole corner applauding, color story: milk crate cobalt and summer stoop gold over ink black

name: The Hydrant Who Wanted August Back
brief: A fire hydrant on a snowbound Mott Haven corner opens itself in February and throws a summer rainbow arc over a block of parked cars, kids in puffer coats running out with no shoes on, eye flowers blooming in the freezing spray, color story: hydrant fire red and February snow blue white over ink black

name: The Mailbox Kept One Letter
brief: A blue street mailbox on an Astoria corner refuses to release a single envelope to the collection truck, holding it back in a hinged mouth while the carrier stares, an eye flower opening in the slot, the letter glowing faintly through the paper, color story: mailbox postal blue and envelope cream over ink black

name: The Newsstand That Reads Aloud
brief: A shuttered subway entrance newsstand flips its own magazines open in sequence and reads the day to a blind commuter who stops to listen, pages fanning like wings, eye flowers opening in the folds of the paper, morning crowd blurring past them both, color story: newsprint gray and morning platform amber over ink black

name: The Bike Rack Locked Itself
brief: A West Village bike rack curls a steel arm around a bicycle a thief is walking away with and simply will not let go, the thief tugging in disbelief, eye flowers opening in the galvanised loops, cobblestones wet and reflecting everything, color story: rack galvanised silver and cobblestone slate over ink black

name: The Bench With a Long Memory
brief: A Riverside Park bench slides its own armrest divider aside so a tired man can lie down, its wooden slats carrying the ghost impressions of every person who ever sat there, eye flowers opening in the grain, river light moving on the underside, color story: bench slat brown and Hudson evening blue over ink black

name: The Streetlight Bent Down
brief: A streetlight on a dark East New York block bends its neck like a swan to put its light exactly where a woman is walking, following her step for step, eye flowers opening in the sodium lamp housing, the rest of the block still in shadow, color story: sodium lamp gold and block shadow indigo over ink black

name: The Scaffolding Light Sings
brief: The caged bulbs strung under a Financial District sidewalk shed begin blinking in perfect rhythm to a busker below them, becoming a lighting rig for a concert nobody planned, eye flowers opening in each cage, commuters slowing without knowing why, color story: caged bulb tungsten and shed plywood tan over ink black

name: The Manhole Cover Salutes
brief: A cast iron manhole cover on Lafayette Street rises on a column of steam, hovers, and tips forward in an unmistakable bow to a sanitation worker ending her shift, the casting pattern rearranged into a living iris, color story: cast iron black and steam column gold over ink black

name: The Awning Wakes the Block
brief: A vinyl awning over a Jackson Heights storefront shakes itself out at sunrise and every awning down the avenue answers in a rolling wave of colour, eye flowers opening along each scalloped edge, shopkeepers coming out one by one to watch it pass, color story: awning crimson and Queens sunrise gold over ink black

name: The First Blink of the Grid
brief: Seen from a helicopter above Midtown at blue hour, every machine and object in New York opens an eye at the same instant: ten thousand traffic signals, every window, every hydrant, every parked car, every antenna and water tower and screen, the entire grid blinking once in unison so that the island itself reads as one vast living iris, a single tiny figure on a rooftop with both arms raised, eye flowers erupting from the avenues in blooming waves of light, color story: citywide blink cyan gold and blue hour cobalt over ink black

name: The Turnstile Waves People Through
brief: A subway turnstile at a Brooklyn station spins its own arms freely and ushers a mother with a stroller and three exhausted workers through without a swipe, eye flowers opening in the card reader slot, the station agent looking away on purpose, color story: turnstile steel and station tile cream over ink black

name: The R Train Takes the Long Way
brief: An old subway car detaches from its schedule and carries eleven riders on a route that does not exist, tunnel walls opening into a cavern of hanging eye flowers, the riders pressed to the windows with their phones forgotten in their hands, color story: train car burnt orange and tunnel bloom violet over ink black

name: The Countdown Clock Lies Kindly
brief: A platform countdown clock quietly adds two minutes so a sprinting teenager can make her train, the digits reforming into a slow blinking eye flower as she clears the doors, the whole platform in motion blur around her, color story: clock display amber and platform tile white over ink black

name: The MetroCard Machine Confesses
brief: A fare machine in a Bronx mezzanine spits back every coin it has ever swallowed in a bright avalanche onto the floor, commuters kneeling to gather it, an enormous apologetic eye flower opening across its screen, color story: coin silver and mezzanine fluorescent green over ink black

name: The Emergency Brake Thinks It Over
brief: The red emergency brake handle in a crowded car considers being pulled by a panicking tourist and gently pulls itself back up, the whole car exhaling at once, an eye flower opening in the handle housing, straps swaying in unison, color story: brake handle red and car interior stainless over ink black

name: The Escalator That Never Worked
brief: The permanently broken escalator at a deep Washington Heights station shudders to life for one minute at three in the morning and carries a single stunned man up into the light, eye flowers opening between every tread, tiled arch glowing above, color story: escalator steel and station arch amber over ink black

name: The Bus Kneels for Everyone
brief: A city bus on a Flatbush avenue kneels lower than it was ever built to, all the way to the curb, and waits with its doors open for a man with a walker who is still half a block away, eye flowers opening in the door glass, rain beading on the windshield, color story: bus transit blue and rainy avenue gray over ink black

name: The Ferry Turned to Look
brief: The Staten Island ferry stops mid harbour and rotates its whole orange bulk to face the skyline for a full minute, hundreds of passengers pouring to one rail, eye flowers opening in the wake foam and along the deck rivets, gulls hanging still in the air, color story: ferry orange and harbour dusk pewter over ink black

name: The Tram Cable Held On
brief: The Roosevelt Island tram cable visibly tightens its braided steel like a tensed muscle as a gust hits the car over the East River, passengers gripping straps, eye flowers opening along the cable strands, the Queensboro Bridge lit below, color story: cable steel silver and East River twilight blue over ink black

name: The Citi Bike That Went Home
brief: A share bike breaks its dock at midnight and rides itself back to the block where it was assembled, pedals turning with no rider, eye flowers opening in the basket and both wheels, empty avenue stretching ahead under a green wave of lights, color story: share bike blue and empty avenue sodium gold over ink black

name: The Taxi With One Last Fare
brief: A retired yellow cab rolls out of a Long Island City lot on its own and picks up an elderly woman standing at a corner where a stand has not existed in thirty years, an eye flower opening in the roof light, meter glowing without being started, color story: taxi yellow and pre dawn violet over ink black

name: The Rail Yard Choir
brief: Two hundred parked subway cars in a Coney Island rail yard open their doors in unison at dawn and hum one enormous chord that rattles every window in the neighbourhood, eye flowers opening in every doorway, one night worker standing on the catwalk in tears, color story: rail yard rust and dawn haze rose over ink black

name: The Signal Tower Confesses Delays
brief: An ancient interlocking signal tower over a junction throws all its brass levers at once and finally routes every train correctly for the first time in decades, eye flowers opening on every lever knob, the operator sitting back with his hands in the air, color story: brass lever gold and tower window green over ink black

name: The Bike Lane Redrew Itself
brief: The painted green bike lane on a Manhattan avenue lifts off the asphalt like a ribbon and re routes itself around a double parked truck, cyclists following the floating path in single file, eye flowers opening along the paint edge, color story: bike lane green and avenue asphalt slate over ink black

name: The Subway Map Rearranged
brief: The wall map in a station mezzanine reorders its own coloured lines into the shape of a flower with every station dot as a living iris, a lost tourist and a lifelong rider standing shoulder to shoulder trying to read it, color story: transit map primary red and station tile white over ink black

name: The Last Car at Coney
brief: The final car of the last train pulls into the elevated Coney Island terminal and its rear window turns into an enormous open eye watching the Atlantic, a single conductor on the platform saluting it, eye flowers opening in the salt corroded steel, color story: terminal steel green and Atlantic night black blue over ink black

name: The Conductor's Window
brief: The small sliding window of a train operator's cab opens on its own and the whole cab leans out to look at a kid on the platform waving with total commitment, an eye flower opening in the window frame, headlight throwing the boy's shadow forty feet down the tile, color story: cab window steel and headlight white gold over ink black

name: The Third Rail Went Quiet
brief: The third rail powers itself down and lies harmless while a track worker retrieves a dropped phone, its cover plate blooming into an eye flower that watches him climb back up, tunnel lights receding into a vanishing point behind, color story: third rail cover ochre and tunnel dark teal over ink black

name: The Announcement Nobody Understood
brief: A platform speaker finally makes itself perfectly clear for one sentence and an entire rush hour crowd stops dead and turns toward it as one body, eye flowers opening in the speaker grille, the sound visible as concentric rings in the dust, color story: speaker grille gray and rush hour amber over ink black

name: The Bus Shelter Grew a Roof
brief: A half broken bus shelter in a Queens downpour extends its glass roof twice its length to cover eight people who did not fit, eye flowers opening in the ad frame where a poster used to be, rain sheeting off the new edge in a curtain, color story: shelter glass green and downpour silver over ink black

name: The Ticket Gate Remembers Grandpa
brief: A commuter rail gate at a Bronx station holds itself open for a young man carrying his grandfather's old briefcase, recognising something it has no business recognising, an eye flower opening in the reader panel, station clock frozen behind him, color story: gate brushed steel and station clock brass over ink black

name: The Elevator That Chose Floors
brief: A station elevator ignores every button and delivers a man to the exact platform he actually needed, doors opening onto a train already waiting, eye flowers opening in the button panel, his reflection multiplied in the brushed walls, color story: elevator steel and platform light gold over ink black

name: The Track Bed Garden
brief: The gravel and litter of a track bed under a Queens elevated line erupts into a dense wild garden of eye flowers overnight, a track inspector standing in the middle of it with his flashlight lowered, sun coming through the girders in slats, color story: track ballast gray and bloom magenta over ink black

name: The Whole Car Turned Around
brief: Every seat in a subway car rotates to face a busker mid song and stays there, the riders too surprised to pretend otherwise, eye flowers opening in the seat moulding and every ceiling panel, poles bending slightly toward the music, color story: seat orange and car fluorescent white over ink black

name: The Claw Machine Lets Go
brief: A rigged claw machine in a Chinatown arcade grips properly for once and hands a stuffed animal down to a kid who spent his last four dollars, an eye flower opening in the claw's knuckle, arcade light strobing across a hundred plush faces, color story: arcade neon magenta and plush toy cream over ink black

name: The Snack Machine Drops Two
brief: A hospital basement vending machine drops a second bag for a woman on hour nineteen of a waiting room, the coil turning one extra revolution deliberately, eye flowers opening behind the glass, corridor light stretching away empty, color story: vending glass blue and corridor fluorescent green over ink black

name: The Photo Booth Waited Years
brief: An analog photo booth in a Williamsburg bar fires all four flashes for a couple who broke up in it a decade ago and just walked back in separately, an eye flower opening in the lens hood, the strip developing in real time with impossible images, color story: flash white and curtain velvet red over ink black

name: The Gumball Machine Counts
brief: A dusty gumball globe in a hardware store lobby releases exactly the colour a child silently wished for, every time, for eleven children in a row, eye flowers opening among the gumballs, the owner watching from behind a wall of keys, color story: gumball primary spectrum and hardware store brown over ink black

name: The Laundry Machine Sings Off Balance
brief: An overloaded washer in an Inwood laundromat goes so far off balance it walks three feet across the floor and the entire room starts clapping on its rhythm, eye flowers opening in the porthole door, suds sliding across tile, color story: suds white and laundromat mint green over ink black

name: The Newspaper Box Opened Free
brief: A rusted sidewalk newspaper box springs its door on a February morning and hands out its last yellowed papers to anyone who wants one, eye flowers opening in the coin mechanism, wind taking a single sheet up past a bank of windows, color story: box red enamel and newsprint yellow gray over ink black

name: The Toll Booth Waved
brief: An automated toll gantry over a bridge approach lifts its arm and waves a moving truck through on the day a family is leaving the city for good, eye flowers opening in the sensor housing, the skyline filling the rearview mirror, color story: gantry steel and bridge sunset amber over ink black

name: The Parking Meter Forgave
brief: A muni meter on a Park Slope street reprints a receipt with two extra hours as a delivery driver sprints back, an eye flower opening in the printer slot, ticket agent one car away and slowing down, color story: meter dark green and receipt paper white over ink black

name: The Jukebox Skipped the Ad
brief: A digital jukebox in an Astoria dive refuses forty dollars of queue skips and plays the song a woman at the end of the bar picked an hour ago, eye flowers opening in the illuminated panel, the bar going quiet in stages, color story: jukebox neon violet and bar mahogany over ink black

name: The Cash Register Rounded Down
brief: A steel register in a Sunset Park grocery drops the total by exactly the amount a shopper was short and slams its drawer shut before anyone can argue, an eye flower opening in the drawer, the line behind saying nothing, color story: register steel and grocery fluorescent gold over ink black

name: The Card Reader Cheers
brief: A card reader in a Lower East Side wine shop displays a small triumphant animation of blooming eye flowers when a first time business owner's card finally goes through, her hands still on the counter, color story: reader screen cyan and shop bottle green over ink black

name: The Vending Wall at Three
brief: A wall of eight vending machines in an empty office lobby at three in the morning lights up in sequence like a chorus line for a lone security guard doing his rounds, eye flowers opening in every product coil, marble floor mirroring all of it, color story: vending glow spectrum and lobby marble cream over ink black

name: The Pizza Oven Knows Sunday
brief: A coal fired oven in a Bleecker Street shop turns its own pies with a stone arm and refuses to burn a single one during the Sunday rush, an eye flower opening in the fire mouth, flour hanging in the light like weather, color story: oven ember orange and flour dust cream over ink black

name: The Dumpling Steamer Stack
brief: A tower of bamboo steamers in a Flushing kitchen lifts its own lids in a rolling wave releasing a wall of steam that fills the whole frame, eye flowers opening in every rising cloud, cooks stopped mid motion around it, color story: bamboo tan and steam pearl white over ink black

name: The Bagel Kettle at Dawn
brief: A boiling kettle in an Upper West Side bagel shop flips its own rings at four in the morning with impossible precision, water throwing arcs of light, eye flowers opening in the rolling boil, the baker standing back with folded arms, color story: kettle steel and boiling water gold over ink black

name: The Espresso Machine Pulled Perfect
brief: A brass espresso machine in a Carroll Gardens cafe pulls a flawless shot for a barista on her first solo shift, crema forming into a small eye flower in the cup, morning light hitting the group heads, color story: brass machine gold and crema hazel over ink black

name: The Fryer Made a Decision
brief: A deep fryer in a Sheepshead Bay kitchen lifts its own basket clear before a distracted cook loses a hand, oil suspended in a fan of droplets, an eye flower opening in the vapour above the vat, the cook frozen with his eyes closed, color story: fryer oil amber and kitchen steel over ink black

name: The Walk In Kept the Cake
brief: A restaurant walk in freezer seals itself against a power cut and holds one wedding cake at exactly the right temperature through eleven hours of darkness, eye flowers opening in the frost on every shelf, one emergency bulb burning, color story: frost blue white and emergency bulb red over ink black

name: The Cutting Board Confessed
brief: A scarred wooden board in a Lower East Side kitchen shows every cut ever made on it as a glowing map of a career, the chef running his thumb across it, eye flowers opening in the deepest grooves, service noise blurred behind the pass, color story: board maple gold and knife scar silver over ink black

name: The Dishwasher Took a Break
brief: An industrial dish machine in a Midtown basement shuts its own hood and simply stops for four minutes so the actual dishwasher can sit down, eye flowers opening in the steam vent, the whole pit quiet for the first time all night, color story: dish pit steam white and basement tile green over ink black

name: The Cart of Ice at Fulton
brief: A fish market ice cart at Hunts Point pushes itself down the wet aisle at four in the morning, shovels riding on top, eye flowers opening in the crushed ice among the catch, breath fogging under the sodium lamps, color story: crushed ice blue white and market sodium orange over ink black

name: The Coffee Cart Rolled Uphill
brief: A blue and white paper cup cart climbs a Murray Hill grade on its own while its owner jogs behind laughing, an eye flower opening in the urn spout, morning commuters parting for it, color story: cart cobalt and paper cup white over ink black

name: The Slice Counter Sang
brief: The heat lamps over a Penn Station slice counter hum a chord and every pizza under them turns to face a man eating alone at eleven at night, eye flowers opening in the lamp housings, tiles reflecting orange, color story: heat lamp orange and counter tile white over ink black

name: The Roti Press
brief: A press in a Richmond Hill kitchen turns out rotis in a rhythm a grandmother recognises as her mother's exact timing and she has to hold the counter, eye flowers opening in the browning surface, flour smoke rising in a shaft of window light, color story: roti golden brown and kitchen window white over ink black

name: The Cuchifrito Window
brief: A steam table window on a Bronx avenue slides open by itself for a man who lost his job an hour ago and pushes a full plate across, eye flowers opening in the sneeze guard glass, avenue reflected in the chrome behind him, color story: steam table gold and avenue evening blue over ink black

name: The Bialy Oven Refused to Close
brief: A century old bakery oven on the Lower East Side keeps its door propped and its fire lit on the night the shop was supposed to close forever, eye flowers opening in the brick arch, the owner and his daughter standing in the heat, color story: oven brick red and firelight gold over ink black

name: The Noodle Puller's Hands
brief: A pair of mechanical arms in a Flushing noodle shop pull dough into a hundred strands in one motion, flour bursting outward in a halo, eye flowers opening in the swinging loops, the whole counter filming, color story: dough cream and flour burst white over ink black

name: The Egg Cream Fountain
brief: A soda fountain in a Brighton Beach luncheonette pulls its own lever and builds a perfect egg cream with a head like a cloud for a man who ordered nothing, eye flowers opening in the foam, chrome curving the whole room into the shot, color story: fountain chrome and egg cream foam white over ink black

name: The Jerk Drum Smoked All Night
brief: A halved oil drum grill on a Flatbush sidewalk keeps its own fire perfect from dusk to dawn while its pitmaster sleeps in a folding chair beside it, eye flowers opening in the smoke, a line of people waiting patiently for him to wake, color story: charcoal ember red and dawn smoke gray over ink black

name: The Tortilla Comal
brief: A comal in a Sunset Park kitchen flips tortillas into the air in a slow arc that hangs impossibly long, eye flowers opening in each browned circle, the family kitchen crowded and every face turned up, color story: comal iron black and masa gold over ink black

name: The Cannoli Case
brief: A refrigerated pastry case on Arthur Avenue lights itself and rotates its trays to present exactly the thing a grieving customer needed, eye flowers opening in the curved glass, brass edging catching the shop light, color story: pastry cream ivory and case brass gold over ink black

name: The Rice Cooker Waited Up
brief: A rice cooker on a Jackson Heights counter holds warm past midnight for a daughter working a double, its lid steam curling into the shape of a hand, an eye flower opening in the vent, apartment dark except one bulb, color story: rice white and kitchen bulb amber over ink black

name: The Kimchi Fridge Speaks
brief: A dedicated fridge in a Murray Hill Korean grocery hums a lullaby at a frequency only the owner's mother used to sing, jars glowing faintly, eye flowers opening in the brine, aisle stretching away in cold light, color story: kimchi crimson and fridge light cyan over ink black

name: The Bodega Grill Cheese Miracle
brief: A flat top makes a grilled cheese so perfect that a hungover man on a stool at eight in the morning puts his head down on the counter in gratitude, eye flowers opening in the melt, morning light cutting through the window bars, color story: cheddar gold and counter formica yellow over ink black

name: The Catering Tray Multiplied
brief: A single aluminium tray at a church basement dinner keeps producing food long after it should be empty, servers looking at each other over it, eye flowers opening in the steam holes, folding tables stretching back into the dark, color story: aluminium tray silver and basement gold over ink black

name: The Kitchen Bell Rang Itself
brief: The expo bell in a Tribeca kitchen rings at the exact second the last ticket clears on the hardest night of the year and the entire line stops and looks at it, eye flowers opening in the dome, heat shimmer over the pass, color story: bell chrome and heat lamp gold over ink black

name: The Billboard Turned Around
brief: An enormous Times Square screen rotates on its mounts to face away from the tourists and toward a single fire escape in Hell's Kitchen where a girl is drawing, its whole surface becoming one slow blinking eye flower, the crowd below all turned the wrong way, color story: screen spectrum white and Hell's Kitchen brick over ink black

name: The Bodega TV Plays the Game
brief: A tiny wall mounted television behind a counter refuses to switch off during the ninth inning and eleven strangers crowd the aisle to watch, eye flowers opening in the screen static, the cat asleep across the top of it, color story: screen phosphor green and bodega gold over ink black

name: The Phone That Stayed Down
brief: Every phone in a crowded subway car goes dark at once and forces two hundred people to look at each other for eleven full seconds, eye flowers opening in every black screen, faces caught in genuine surprise, color story: dead screen black mirror and car fluorescent white over ink black

name: The Bus Shelter Ad Waved
brief: A backlit shelter poster of a model raises her hand and waves at a kid waiting for the bus, breaking every rule of what a poster is, an eye flower opening where the product would be, rain on the glass, color story: poster backlight white and rain glass silver over ink black

name: The Elevator Screen Told a Joke
brief: The little news screen in a Midtown elevator abandons its feed and tells one perfect joke, breaking eleven strangers in suits into helpless laughter between floors, eye flowers opening at the screen corners, brushed steel doubling every face, color story: screen cyan and elevator steel over ink black

name: The Projector on the Brick
brief: A guerrilla projector in a Bushwick alley throws a film onto a brick wall and the bricks themselves start participating, mortar lines rearranging into eye flowers, forty people sitting on crates and car hoods watching, color story: projector beam white and alley brick rust over ink black

name: The Jumbotron Found One Face
brief: An arena scoreboard screen ignores twenty thousand people and holds on one exhausted single father in the upper deck for a full minute until the whole building is chanting for a man they have never met, eye flowers opening across the pixel grid, color story: jumbotron white blue and arena seat maroon over ink black

name: The Bootleg Stream
brief: A cracked laptop on a Ridgewood coffee table plays a fight through eleven layers of buffering to nine people packed on one couch, the pixellation itself blooming into eye flowers, everyone leaning the same direction, color story: buffer pixel cyan and living room lamp amber over ink black

name: The Ring Camera Blinked Back
brief: A doorbell camera on a Ditmas Park porch turns to follow a package thief down the entire block, its lens becoming a furious living iris, porch lights snapping on ahead of him one by one, color story: porch light gold and night lawn green black over ink black

name: The Group Chat Rendered
